key_insight: Competing Ge-driven off-centering and Sn-favored octahedral tilting create a low-temperature phase boundary at x = 0.60–0.65 in lead-free CsGe₁₋ₓSnₓBr₃ alloys.
engineering_relevance: Ge/Sn mixing offers a route to tune polar order, structural phases, and band gaps in lead-free perovskites relevant to solar-cell materials design.
method: Train a charge-aware machine-learned interatomic potential on hybrid-functional data.
Run large-scale molecular dynamics across the full Ge/Sn composition range.
Map composition–temperature phases and associated band-gap changes.
evidence_signal: Simulations reproduce both end members’ known transition sequences and temperatures, reveal an intermediate I4/mcm phase, and show a low-temperature band-gap jump versus smooth composition dependence at 350 K.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational structural and electronic predictions, not experimental alloy validation or solar-cell performance.
paper_title: Competing Octahedral Tilting and $B$-Site Off-Centering Govern the Phase Diagram of CsGe$_{1-x}$Sn$_x$Br$_3$ Perovskite Alloys
